comparison: Perfect match on clinical findings (C10, C57). Both evaluations support the correlation between lipid levels and drug resistance in human VL patients. OpenEval provides explicit validation while peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the 'compelling evidence' for the overall hypothesis.

Strong agreement on drug resistance mechanisms (C9, C52-C56, C95). Both evaluations support the lipid-mediated drug resistance findings and aspirin's beneficial effect. OpenEval emphasizes the causal evidence from lipid droplet reduction, while peer reviewers explicitly discuss aspirin's effect on antimony resistance.

Strong agreement on NPC-1 suppression and SREBP2 regulation (C6, C7, C42-C45, C103). Both evaluations support these findings. Peer reviewers note the mechanism remains an open question regarding translational control, while OpenEval emphasizes the convergent evidence from multiple experimental approaches.

Strong agreement on lipid dependency (C25-C27, C96). Both evaluations support the differential effects on LD-R versus LD-S under various lipid conditions. Peer reviewers describe the evidence as 'compelling' for the hypothesis that parasites have developed enhanced capacity to acquire and utilize lipids.

Strong agreement on enhanced replication phenotype (C23, C24, C62). Both evaluations support the logarithmic growth between 4-24 hours. Peer reviewers describe this as 'a puzzling observation for which they provide compelling evidence' and note the unexplained slowdown after 24 hours.

Strong agreement on fluid-phase endocytosis mechanism (C4, C34-C38, C98). Both evaluations support the LDL uptake mechanism. Peer reviewers affirm the authors 'present compelling evidence that supports their hypothesis' about lipid acquisition capacity.

Agreement on LDL-vesicle fusion with PV (C39, C40). OpenEval emphasizes temporal progression at 4hr and 24hr timepoints. Peer reviewers note the 'novel observation' of increased Lamp1 expression as early as 4 hours with LD-R, treating this as validated.

Agreement on elevated lipid accumulation (C29-C33). OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence from multiple analytical techniques. Peer reviewers support this as part of the 'compelling evidence' for the lipid scavenging hypothesis, though they focus more on the overall mechanism than specific techniques.

Agreement on selective lipid accumulation (C5, C47-C49, C94). Both evaluations support the selective recruitment of neutral lipids while excluding oxidized-LDL. Peer reviewers note this 'adds to other work that has implicated pathogen-derived processes in the selective recruitment of vesicles.'

Agreement on lipid droplet accumulation (C8, C50, C51). OpenEval emphasizes consistency across multiple imaging modalities. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the overall 'compelling evidence' for lipid utilization mechanisms.

Agreement on background context regarding drug resistance (C72-C76). Both evaluations support this established literature. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge that 'resistant parasites are now a distinct strain' and validate the background context.

Agreement on foundational concepts (C1, C2, C17-C20, C58, C93). OpenEval categorizes these as supporting context from prior literature. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these as the foundation for the study's hypothesis about lipid acquisition capacity.

Agreement on clinical and biological context (C12, C13). Both evaluations support the background establishing LD-R as a persistent phenotype. Peer reviewers acknowledge the circulation of resistant parasites as evidence of a distinct strain.

Agreement on biological rationale (C17-C19, C93). OpenEval treats these as well-established facts providing rationale for investigating lipid metabolism. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these foundational concepts when acknowledging the study's hypothesis.

Agreement on mechanistic framework (C77-C87). Both evaluations support these established biological concepts from prior literature. OpenEval emphasizes they provide the mechanistic framework for interpretation. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these as part of the overall evidence base.

Agreement on differential lipid acquisition timing (C28). OpenEval supports this with Figure 3 data showing no difference at early timepoints. Peer reviewers do not explicitly challenge this observation, accepting it as part of the 'compelling evidence.'

Agreement on methodological justification (C60, C61, C64-C67). OpenEval supports these as establishing KCs as an appropriate model system. Peer reviewers implicitly accept the methodological choices as part of the overall study design.

Agreement on biological relationships (C69, C70, C88). OpenEval treats these as known relationships from prior literature. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these as part of the mechanistic framework, though they note some mechanisms remain open questions.

Agreement on persistent aggressive phenotype (C89). Both evaluations support this interpretive conclusion. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'It is of interest to determine the properties that favor the retention of their drug resistance phenotype,' acknowledging the persistent nature.

Both mark as uncertain/speculative (C90, C99, C101, C102, C104-C106). OpenEval notes these lack direct experimental validation and are explicitly marked as speculation. Peer reviewers note 'the genetic basis for the parasite's gluttony for lipids remains unresolved' and mechanisms are 'open questions,' indicating uncertainty about underlying mechanisms despite accepting phenotypic observations.

Partial overlap on initial infection characteristics (C22, C63). OpenEval supports no difference in initial attachment. Peer reviewers do not explicitly discuss this but accept the overall characterization of LD-R behavior as supported by 'compelling evidence.'

Minimal overlap on inflammatory response (C46). OpenEval supports cytokine measurement findings. Peer reviewers do not explicitly discuss this specific finding but include it in the overall body of 'compelling' evidence.

Minimal overlap on background context (C15, C16). OpenEval treats these as establishing clinical context. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these as foundational information without explicit discussion.

Minimal overlap on evolutionary adaptation speculation (C91). OpenEval notes this involves speculation about evolutionary adaptation. Peer reviewers accept the drug resistance findings but do not explicitly address evolutionary interpretations.
